title: Selective Isolation of TOP3B•mRNA Covalent Intermediates Using Denaturing Oligo-dT Pulldown
author: Julia E. Warrick
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare buffers and add DTT
steps.instruction: Make oligo‑dT lysis, wash I, wash II, low‑salt, and elution (TE) buffers according to the Recipes; filter each through a 0.22 µm cellulose‑nitrate vacuum filter, store at room temperature, and add fresh DTT to lysis and wash I buffers to a final 5 mM immediately before use (e.g., 700 µL lysis buffer and 1 mL wash I buffer per sample).

steps.title: Transfect Neuro‑2A cells
steps.instruction: Twenty‑four hours before collection, transfect Neuro‑2A cells in a 6‑well plate (≈1 × 10⁶ cells per well) with plasmids encoding WT or mutant TOP3B‑3xFLAG using your preferred reagent (e.g., Lipofectamine or FuGENE 4K).

steps.title: Wash cells with ice‑cold PBS
steps.instruction: At ~80 % confluence, aspirate media and gently wash each well with 1 mL ice‑cold 1× PBS; aspirate the PBS.

steps.title: Lyse cells with oligo‑dT buffer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL oligo‑dT lysis buffer (with 5 mM DTT) directly to each well, shake the plate on an orbital shaker at maximum speed for 10 min at room temperature, then transfer the lysate to a pre‑labeled 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Pipette up and down in the well several times before transfer to improve recovery.
Pause point: lysates may be stored at –80 °C until the next step.

steps.title: Reduce lysate viscosity by syringing
steps.instruction: Pass each lysate once through a 28 G needle attached to a syringe (1× pass; optional second pass for very confluent cells, but do not exceed 3 passes).

steps.title: Prepare oligo‑dT magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Label four 1.7 mL tubes per sample and place one tube per sample on a DynaMag‑2 magnetic rack; bring beads to room temperature, aliquot 100 µL beads into each tube, add 200 µL oligo‑dT lysis buffer (with DTT), invert gently for 2 min, spin briefly (~1 s), then incubate on the magnet for 2 min.

substeps.instruction: If using a p200 tip, cut off the tip tip to avoid shearing beads.

steps.title: Bind lysate to beads
steps.instruction: While beads remain on the magnet, remove the supernatant, then add the entire volume of syringed lysate to the beads, resuspend by pipetting up/down 5×, and rotate end‑over‑end at 15 rpm for 30 min at room temperature (incubation can be reduced to 10 min if necessary).

steps.title: Wash beads with wash I buffer
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a mini‑centrifuge for ~1 s, then on the magnet for 2 min; discard supernatant, add 500 µL oligo‑dT wash I buffer (with 5 mM DTT), resuspend 4–5×, invert 1 min, spin ~1 s, magnet 2 min, discard; repeat wash I once more (total two washes).

steps.title: Wash beads with wash II buffer
steps.instruction: Remove from magnet, add 500 µL oligo‑dT wash II buffer (no DTT), resuspend 2–3×, invert 1 min, spin ~1 s, magnet 2 min, discard; repeat wash II once more (total two washes).

steps.title: Final low‑salt wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL oligo‑dT low‑salt buffer, resuspend 2–3×, invert 1 min, spin ~1 s, magnet 2 min, discard supernatant (beads may move slowly after this step).

steps.title: Elute RNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL oligo‑dT elution (TE) buffer, resuspend 2×, vortex 2–3 s, heat at 50 °C with 300 rpm agitation for 2 min, spin ~1 s, magnet 2 min, transfer 195 µL supernatant to a fresh tube (avoid beads), spin at 18 000 rcf for 5 min at room temperature, then transfer 185 µL to a final tube, place on ice; samples may be used immediately or stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare membranes for slot blot
steps.instruction: Cut one nitrocellulose membrane and two positively charged nylon membranes to size, cut the bottom‑left corner of each for orientation, and incubate all three in 20 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.4 for 1 h at room temperature (ensure full submersion).

steps.title: Quantify and denature RNA
steps.instruction: Measure RNA concentration with a Nanodrop, dilute each sample to 2 µg RNA in 200 µL 1× PBS in a sterile PCR strip, invert gently, spin briefly, then heat‑denature at 70 °C for 15 min in a thermal cycler.

steps.title: Assemble slot‑blot apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the apparatus on a raised platform, connect to a vacuum source via a three‑way stopcock (keep valve closed), remove the top piece, lay two nylon membranes followed by the nitrocellulose membrane (nitrocellulose on top) onto the slots, remove bubbles with a blot roller or serological pipette, wipe edges with a Kimwipe, replace the top piece, and tighten screws in an X pattern (hand‑tighten only).

substeps.instruction: If using a Bio‑Rad apparatus, insert two filter‑paper pieces (pre‑equilibrated in 20 mM Tris‑HCl) beneath the membranes.

steps.title: Pre‑wash membranes
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add 195 µL 20 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.4 to each slot, apply full vacuum to draw through, repeat once more (total two washes). Keep the valve closed after each wash to avoid drying.

steps.title: Load RNA samples and wash
steps.instruction: With the valve closed, add 195 µL of each denatured RNA sample to its slot (recommended to start in lane 2), fill remaining empty slots with 195 µL 20 mM Tris‑HCl, apply vacuum to draw samples through, then wash once with 195 µL 20 mM Tris‑HCl using the same procedure.

steps.title: Disassemble apparatus and mark slots
steps.instruction: Leave vacuum on, loosen screws in reverse order, remove the top piece onto a clean surface, and immediately pencil‑mark the slots surrounding each sample (e.g., mark lanes 1 and 7 if samples are in lanes 2‑6).

steps.title: Block nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: While vacuum remains on, lift the nitrocellulose membrane with forceps and place it in a container containing 5 % (w/v) non‑fat dry milk; block for 30 min at room temperature with orbital shaking, then wash 3 × with TBST (10 × TBS, 0.1 % Tween‑20).

steps.title: Cut and incubate nitrocellulose with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Cut the membrane around the penciled slots using a fresh, 70 % ethanol‑cleaned razor blade (remove the entire perimeter edge), fold onto plastic wrap, place in a blot box with mouse anti‑FLAG M2 antibody diluted 1:1 000 in primary‑antibody solution, and incubate overnight on a rocker at 4 °C.

steps.title: Process top nylon membrane (methylene blue)
steps.instruction: Remove the top nylon membrane with forceps, place on a paper towel, UV‑crosslink at 120 000 µJ/cm² (Stratalinker 1800), incubate in methylene blue staining solution (0.2 % w/v methylene blue, 0.4 M acetic acid, 0.4 M sodium acetate) for 20 min at room temperature with shaking, save the stain for reuse, wash 2 × 1–2 min with distilled water on a shaker until background is cleared, and image the stained membrane as a loading control.

steps.title: Clean slot‑blot apparatus
steps.instruction: Turn off vacuum, dismantle the apparatus, wash the middle and top parts with a small amount of dish soap and distilled water, rinse the bottom part with distilled water only, and dry (air‑dry the Bio‑Rad version; Kimwipe‑dry the Hoefer version).

steps.title: Day 2: Wash nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: Place the nitrocellulose membrane (from primary antibody) into ~30 mL TBST and shake for 10 min at room temperature; repeat for a total of three 10‑minute washes.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Add HRP‑conjugated goat anti‑mouse IgG (1:30 000 dilution) in secondary‑antibody solution, incubate for 1 h at room temperature with shaking.

steps.title: Final TBST washes
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST as in the previous wash step, shaking at room temperature.

steps.title: Dry membrane and develop chemiluminescence
steps.instruction: Pick up the membrane by a corner, let it drip‑dry 5–10 s, place on a flat plastic film, incubate with 2 mL SuperSignal West Pico PLUS substrate for 5 min at room temperature, briefly drip‑dry excess reagent, wrap the membrane, and capture chemiluminescence using an Azure Sapphire (or equivalent) imager.
